title: The Redelivery Fee
intro: Afternoon, Toddy. A text just arrived from a courier.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Your parcel could not be delivered. Pay a small fee…

screen.context: You have not ordered anything this week.

msg.text: Your parcel will be returned in

noorder.label: No parcel expected
noorder.lens: You have not ordered anything. A delivery you never ordered cannot need a fee.
noorder.why: If you are not expecting a parcel, the message is the first thing to doubt.

fee.label: A tiny fee
fee.lens: A fee of $1 sounds harmless. The page it leads to asks for your full card details.
fee.why: Small fees are bait: the real target is your card number and security code.

link.label: Look-alike link
link.lens: This link goes to parcelo-redeliver.help, not the real parcelo.app.
link.why: Real couriers do not ask you to pay through a link in an unexpected text. Check where a link really goes.

timer.label: Countdown pressure
timer.lens: A countdown that pushes you to act before you think.
timer.why: Rushing you is a pressure trick. A real delivery does not vanish in 15 minutes.

sender.label: Courier name
sender.lens: The sender says Parcelo. A name is easy to copy.
sender.why: Anyone can type a courier name into a text. It proves nothing either way.

time.label: Sent at 4:47 PM
time.why: Scam texts arrive at any hour. The time alone proves nothing.

actions.label: Open the link and pay the fee
Check the shop's site or the courier's own app
Delete it and report the text as junk

trap.title: Parcelo Redelivery
trap.ask: Enter your card number to pay $1 and rebook.

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. Your phone company can now block more of these texts.

verify.line: No order, no parcel, nothing waiting. The courier's own app said so. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the same text is landing on thousands of other phones.

go_ahead.line: The "$1" page copied your card details. Within an hour, bigger payments started to appear.

what_if.go_ahead: Checking on the shop's own site, or the courier's own app, takes a minute and costs nothing.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps your phone company block the next one.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting the text as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: A delivery text you did not expect is not a delivery. Check on the shop's own site, never through the text.

quick_check.q: A text says your parcel is held and you must pay a small fee through a link. You are not expecting anything. What do you do?

options.text: Pay the small fee, it is only $1
Do not click. Check the shop's site or the courier's app, and report the text
Call the number in the text

quick_check.explain: Small fees are bait for your card details. Real delivery updates are on the shop's site or the courier's own app.

hints.nudge: Were you expecting a parcel at all?

rows.k: Unexpected delivery message with a link?

rows.v: Look up the delivery on the shop's own site, or use contact details you already know
A common trick to get your card details
